bug_semantics: An authenticated attacker can send PUT /api/supplier/{victim_id}. The route has only auth:api middleware and SupplierRequest::authorize() merely checks Auth::check(); SupplierUpdateController then resolves the identifier globally with Supplier::find($id), updates it from $request->all(), and returns the resulting supplier. Because Supplier::$fillable includes company_id while the request rules do not constrain that field and sensitive supplier fields are not hidden, the attacker can read and modify another tenant's supplier and reassign it by supplying company_id.
flaw_origin: The unsafe SupplierUpdateController method body was present but dormant from b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369 (APP_VERSION 4.0.0): neither that revision nor tagged v2.0.1/v4.6.0 registered a supplier PUT API route. The smallest commit that completed the externally reachable vulnerable mechanism was b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403, which imported SupplierUpdateController and added the auth-only PUT /supplier/{id} route while leaving the pre-existing unscoped lookup and mass assignment intact; it set APP_VERSION to 4.15.0.
evidence: Advisory reproduction: GHSA-4hh4-jwxc-xpmf/CVE-2026-78365 names PUT /api/supplier/{id}, cross-tenant Supplier::find($id), $request->all(), attacker-controlled company_id, affected-through 5.3.1, and directly references 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596. BIC search: `git log --all -S"Route::put('/supplier/{id}'" -- routes/api.php` returns only b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403; `git log -L 128,128:routes/api.php b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403` shows that commit adding `Route::put('/supplier/{id}', [SupplierUpdateController::class, 'update'])->middleware(['auth:api'])`. `git show b233f279...` also shows the matching import and version.php changing 4.14.0 to 4.15.0. Direct parent check: `git show 7f05ac6d115c09dc570e002b28e126871057333e:routes/api.php` contains supplier GET/POST/DELETE only and no SupplierUpdateController import or PUT route, while its dormant handler already contains Supplier::find($id) and `$supplier->update($request->all())`; therefore the attack path is absent in the immediate parent. `git grep` at b03c8c6f5fde097cbe44552464c56469b60a4369, v2.0.1, and v4.6.0 likewise finds no supplier PUT route, so history contradicts the advisory's lower 4.0.0 reachability boundary; the source-level vulnerable boundary is 4.15.0 through 5.3.1. Exploit-chain check at b233f279...: SupplierRequest::authorize returns Auth::check(), Supplier::$fillable contains company_id, and the controller globally finds, mass-updates, and returns the record. Fix check: `git show 4a52477e...` changes Supplier::find($id) to a query scoped by Auth::user()->company_id, changes request->all() to request->validated(), and requires update/create supplier permission; version.php changes 5.3.1 to 5.3.2. `git tag --contains 4a52477e...` includes v5.5.3 and v5.14.0, and `git show v5.5.3:version.php` reports 5.5.3, confirming the advisory-linked first tagged fixed release contains the fix. BIC object check: `git cat-file commit b233f279...` shows human author/committer Gustavo Novaro and the exact sole AI trailer quoted in ai_marker; no PR-body, branch, later-commit, or fix marker was used.
reasoning: The unsafe update implementation alone did not make the advisory's API attack possible: Laravel's API routes are explicitly registered in routes/api.php, and the 4.0.0/v2.0.1 and 4.6.0 trees have no supplier PUT registration. Commit b233f27910f32c264243d03021e4f25dbef5f403 is therefore the first complete vulnerable tree: it deliberately publishes the dormant unsafe handler to authenticated users, and its immediate parent lacks that route. This is smaller and causally later than the 2024 aggregate that wrote the dormant method, so no squash decomposition is applicable to the selected BIC. The direct fix 4a52477e6ed66afa436814c80e7bcd68670dd596 closes both tenant selection and mass-assignment paths and strengthens action authorization, with the internal version boundary 5.3.1 to 5.3.2 and tagged v5.5.3 containing it. Because the BIC commit object itself carries the Claude Haiku 4.5 co-author trailer and the BIC first completed the flawed externally reachable mechanism, the BIC-only verdict is AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
